newsitem.title: UK: Shell says confident of French refinery agreement.
newsitem.headline: Shell says confident of French refinery agreement.

text.p: Royal/Dutch Shell Group is confident it can reach an agreement with three other oil companies on how to deal with excess refining capacity in southern France, Shell Group Managing Director Cor Herkstroter said on Thursday.
"I am confident something is going to happen there but I can't be certain...because there are other companies involved," Herkstroter told reporters at a briefing.
Shell in December, announcing the closure of its Swiss Cressier refinery, said it was considering options for the southern France Berre l'Etang plant.
The company said it was in talks with other major oil companies which operate in southern France. Esso France, Total and BP France all run refineries around the port of Marseilles.
An announcement on possible joint rationalisation is being prepared for the French industry ministry by the end of January.
Herkstroter said the French government now was backing its plans after earlier resisting suggestions that some form of refinery rationalisation was necessary.

"We should have been able to move faster, but one of the big problems is in France and I think you've got to bear in mind that in France you can't close a refinery without government approval," Herkstroter said.

"We have made a lot of progress and the government has come to the conclusion that, yes, we have to do something about it and that's very helpful in assisting the process we are going through," he added.
Financial analysts had complained that the measures Shell announced in December fell well short of the restructuring the market had expected.
BP's Lavera refinery in southern France is up for sale but analysts say a coordinated plan to reduce capacity might make the company think again.
